Things you think disqualify you.

They're actually your edge:

"I've only ever worked one job."
Then you know that industry better than anyone starting fresh.

"I failed at 8 side hustles."
Then you know exactly what doesn't work. People pay for that.

"I'm not an expert."
You don't need to be. You need to be 3 steps ahead.

"My story isn't special."
It's specific. Specific sells.

"I'm not techy."
Neither are most of your future customers.

Stop disqualifying yourself. Start counting what you have.

thread: How the 9-5 keeps disciplined people stuck:

1. It pays just enough.
Enough to stay. Never enough to leave.

2. It takes your best energy.
You build your future with what's left.

3. It tells you you're replaceable.
So you never ask what you're worth outside it.

4. It sells you a ladder.
Every rung is the same job with a new title.

5. It makes leaving feel reckless.
When staying with no plan is the real risk.

The way out isn't escaping. It's building.

The scariest thing this Halloween isn't out on the street.

7 things that should actually scare you:

1. Another year exactly like this one.
2. A performance review deciding your future.
3. An AI rollout memo with your team's name on it.
4. Turning 40 with the same plan you had at 30.

5. Savings sitting still while the clock moves.
6. Side hustle #10 ending like #1 through #9.
7. Realizing you had the advantage all along and never used it.

The good news: every one of these is avoidable.

Starting tomorrow.

Follow @bylovemason if you're building your way out.
50 THINGS TO DO INSTEAD OF WASTING ANOTHER YEAR AT YOUR 9-5 (start them tomorrow, November 1):

STOP CHASING:

1. Delete the side hustle courses you never finished.
2. Unfollow every guru selling a model you have no edge in.
3. Stop googling "best business to start".
4. Cancel the tools you paid for before your first sale.
5. Write down every hustle you've tried and what each one cost you.

LOOK AT YOUR CAREER:

6. List every skill your job forced you to master.
7. Write down the 3 problems coworkers always bring to you.
8. Note your best result from the last 5 years.
9. List the software and systems you know cold.
10. Ask what a new hire would pay to learn from you.

LOOK AT YOUR LIFE:

11. Write down the hardest thing you've overcome.
12. List what you've taught yourself with nobody paying you.
13. Ask 3 friends what they come to you for.
14. Note the topic you've watched hundreds of videos on.
15. Write down the transformation others still want.

FIND YOUR UNFAIR ADVANTAGE:

16. Circle where your career and your life overlap.
17. Pick the one you have proof for.
18. Write it in one sentence.
19. Name who it helps: someone 3 years behind you.
20. Name the exact problem it solves for them.

BUILD ONE PRODUCT:

21. Pick one problem, not ten.
22. Choose a simple format: ebook, guide or masterclass.
23. Outline it in one sitting.
24. Give yourself 14 days to finish it.
25. Put a price on it. Free isn't a business.

START CONTENT:

26. Post one lesson from your experience every day.
27. Write to who you were 5 years ago.
28. Share the mistakes, not just the wins.
29. Reply to every comment.
30. Point every post toward your product.

PROTECT YOUR TIME:

31. Block 1 hour a day before or after work. Non-negotiable.
32. Kill one weeknight habit that gives you nothing.
33. Use weekends for building, not recovering.
34. Say no to one extra project at work.
35. Stop checking work messages after hours.

KNOW YOUR NUMBERS:

36. Calculate the monthly number that replaces your salary.
37. Count how many months your savings cover.
38. Cut one expense that doesn't move you forward.
39. Track every dollar the business makes.
40. Measure buyers, not followers.

PLAN YOUR EXIT:

41. Savings and no dependents? Set a date to go all in.
42. People count on you? Build alongside the job.
43. Decide what "holds weight" means in dollars.
44. Tell one person your date.
45. Stop treating your job like your identity.

DO IT NOW:

46. Stop calling your years at work wasted.
47. Stop waiting to feel ready.
48. Stop starting from zero.
49. Save this list.
50. Do number 1 tomorrow. Not Monday. Tomorrow.

thread: The 5 stages of being done with your 9-5:

1. DENIAL
"It's just a bad week."

2. BARGAINING
"If I get the promotion, it'll be fine."

3. ESCAPE
Side hustle after side hustle. Months on each. None of them stick.

4. EXHAUSTION
"Maybe this is just life."

5. CLARITY
You stop looking outside. You realize the business was in your own experience the whole time.

Most people stay stuck between 3 and 4 for years.

Stage 5 is a decision, not something you wait for.
